prompt:
Research the official rate limits of the public GitHub REST API for unauthenticated and authenticated requests. Cite the GitHub documentation page and quote the numbers.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Here are the official rate limits for the public GitHub REST API, based on GitHub's official documentation. Unauthenticated requests have a lower limit per IP address, while authenticated requests have a higher limit per user. Additionally, authenticated requests using OAuth apps or GitHub Apps may have different limits depending on their authorization level.

SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/overview/resources-in-the-rest-api?apiVersion=2022-11-28 | QUOTE: "For unauthenticated requests, the rate limit allows you to make up to 60 requests per hour." | CLAIM: The rate limit for unauthenticated requests to the GitHub REST API is 60 requests per hour.
SOURCE: https://docs.github.com/en/rest/overview/resources-in-the-rest-api?apiVersion=2022-11-28 | QUOTE: "For OAuth apps and personal access tokens, the rate limit is 5,000 requests per hour." | CLAIM: The standard rate limit for authenticated requests (via personal access tokens or OAuth) to the GitHub REST API is 5,000 requests per hour.
